title: refactor(console): retire the system hub card wall; /apps/:app/system lands on the settings hub (objectui#3743)
body:
Fixes #3743
Clause-②: no

A console page and its route go away. `SystemHubPage` is not exported from any published entry. The only export of `@object-ui/console` is `plugin.ts` (`ConsolePlugin`), which does not import it, and the page was never part of `@object-ui/app-shell`.

## What changes

- `apps/console/src/pages/system/SystemHubPage.tsx` (already `@deprecated`) is deleted, with its card array, count queries and badge copy. Its two suites go with it: `SystemHubPage.counts.test.tsx` and `SystemHubPage.metadataCards.test.tsx`.
- The console host's `system` route (the `systemRoutes` fragment in `apps/console/src/AppContent.tsx`) is now `SystemLandingRedirect`. `/apps/:app/system` forwards in one hop to `/apps/:app/system/settings`, the settings hub.
- Comments that cited the deleted page are rewritten: the `SettingsHub.tsx` docblock (the "SystemHubPage look-and-feel" sentence), both `AppContent.tsx` files and five test files.
- `.changeset/3743-retire-system-hub-card-wall.md` bumps `@object-ui/console` by a patch. The only `@object-ui/app-shell` source change is a JSX comment. It compiles to byte-identical JS (evidence below), so app-shell gets no bump.

## Why this landing (the ruling asks for "a navigation/registry-driven entry")

These facts were measured on `origin/main` before any edit:

- **Every navigation declares `system/settings`.**
  - The framework Setup app's `nav_settings_hub` ("All Settings", url `/apps/setup/system/settings`) is in `platform-objects`' `setup-nav.contributions.ts`.
  - `AppSidebar.systemFallbackNavigation` declares it as `sys-config`.
  - `UnifiedSidebar`'s `/home` Administration cluster declares it as `sys-config`.
  - No framework navigation entry targets the bare `/apps/setup/system`. Only objectui's own senders do.
- **The page is driven by a registry.** `SettingsHub` lists the `GET /api/settings` manifests. The framework filters that list per caller: `service-settings` route ledger, "manifests the caller may see, filtered by their capabilities".
- **It renders with zero apps.** The route is in both `DefaultAppContent` route tables, because the fragment is passed as both `extraRoutes` and `extraRoutesNoApp`.
- **Rejected: the app root.** `resolveLandingRoute` picks the app's first navigation entry. With the Setup app present, that is System Overview. With zero apps, though, `/apps/setup` is the "No Apps Configured" empty state, and its "System Settings" button sends the user to `/apps/setup/system`. Redirecting that URL back to the app root would be a loop (the objectui#3590 defect).
- **Rejected: `system/apps`.** It is the first entry of the `sys-*` cluster after the hub itself. But every sender is labelled "System Settings" or "Settings", and AppManagement is app CRUD, not settings.
- No new hand-written list or card array is introduced. The redirect names one route, and the reason for that route is written on the component.

## Every sender of the bare URL still reaches a real page

These senders are unchanged; they all carry `/apps/setup/system`. Each one's href is already pinned beside the sender:

| sender | href pin |
|---|---|
| empty state `go-to-settings-btn` | `packages/app-shell/src/console/__tests__/AppContent.noAppsCta.test.tsx` |
| `sys-settings` in `AppSidebar` and in `UnifiedSidebar` | `packages/app-shell/src/layout/__tests__/systemNavSettingsTarget.test.tsx` |
| `AppSidebar` no-app header and user-menu "Settings" | `packages/app-shell/src/layout/__tests__/appSidebarSettingsTargets.test.tsx` |
| home Quick Action "System Settings" | `packages/app-shell/src/console/home/__tests__/QuickActions.settingsTarget.test.tsx` |
| `ConsoleShell` `SystemRedirect` for a bare `/system` bookmark | `packages/app-shell/src/console/__tests__/systemRedirectTarget.test.tsx` |

Where the URL lands is new, and it is pinned in `apps/console/src/__tests__/AppContent.systemHubRoutes.test.tsx`, in the describe "the bare system landing forwards onto the settings hub (objectui#3743)". The tests use the real host fragment and the real `DefaultAppContent`, and cover:

- one hop with an active app;
- the app prefix is kept;
- one hop with zero apps;
- the zero-app empty-state button, clicked end to end: `/apps/setup` → `/apps/setup/system` → `/apps/setup/system/settings`, with the empty state gone.

## Test-surface handover (H4)

| deleted assertion | disposition | where it is pinned now |
|---|---|---|
| counts suite: the names queried (`sys_organization`, `sys_permission_set`, …), `null` vs `0` badges, one failure blanking one card | **died**: no count surface remains | — |
| (counts suite, implied) those objects are reachable | already on the navigation | `sys-users` / `sys-orgs` / `sys-roles` one-hop object redirects, both branches, in `AppContent.systemHubRoutes.test.tsx` (the `positions` / `permissions` bookmark URLs are pinned in the same file) |
| metadataCards: "Datasources" card → `metadata/datasource` in one hop | **moved**: already pinned on the navigation | `systemNavDatasourcesHop.test.tsx` (both sidebars, zero redirects) |
| metadataCards: CONTROL "Applications" card → `system/apps` | **moved**: already pinned on the navigation | `sys-apps` href in `systemNavSettingsTarget.test.tsx` (both sidebars) |
| metadataCards: "Metadata" card → `metadata` in one hop | **died** with the card | no system-navigation entry declares the directory (the framework Studio app does: `nav_metadata_directory`). The route itself stays pinned by `AppContent.noAppComponentRoutes.test.tsx` and `AppContent.pseudoRouteSegments.test.tsx` |
| metadataCards: MEASUREMENT, byte-identical to the alias hop | **died**: it compared a card with an alias | — |

## Evidence (all on head `0ebfc8ea7` (`git rev-parse --short HEAD`), working tree clean)

**New pins, red on the base and green on the head.**

- Base leg:
  - `git checkout cdefa2a06 -- apps/console/src/AppContent.tsx apps/console/src/pages/system/SystemHubPage.tsx`.
  - On-disk check: `SystemHubPage` mentions in the host = 3, `SystemLandingRedirect` = 0, page present.
  - Result: `Tests  4 failed | 15 passed (19)`. All four failed with `Unable to find an element by: [data-testid="settings-hub-page"]`.
- Restored by a trap:
  - The host blob equals the `HEAD` blob (`1c0c3469`).
  - `git diff HEAD` is 0 bytes, `git status` is clean, and the page is absent.
- Head: `apps/console/` gives `Test Files  114 passed (114)` and `Tests  1261 passed (1261)`.

**Type-check:** `turbo run type-check --filter=@object-ui/console --filter=@object-ui/app-shell` gives `Tasks: 37 successful, 37 total`. The scripts were echoed as `tsc --noEmit && tsc -b tsconfig.node.json --force` (console) and `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` (app-shell). Console's `tsconfig.json` includes `src` with no `exclude`, so the new test file is compiled.

**App-shell tests: a declared narrowing, not the full package.** app-shell has 782 test files; the full package run is left to CI's `Test` shards. The narrowing has two halves:

- **Runtime half.** app-shell's only source change is a JSX comment in `console/AppContent.tsx`. esbuild output of the base and head files has the same sha256 (`843aa2a3…`, 38468 bytes each), so no importer's verdict can move.
- **File-reading half.** Every test outside `apps/console` was run if it names an edited or deleted file, or if it walks, globs or greps the tree (`readdirSync`, glob, `import.meta.glob`, `git ls-files` / `grep`, subprocess). That is 251 files: `Test Files  251 passed (251)`, `Tests  5837 passed (5837)`. The set includes all four edited app-shell tests.
- **Blind spot:** a test that reads one of these files through a path built without the file's name and without walking the tree.

**Gates** (the verdict line each printed; exit 0 unless stated):

- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: "11 source file(s) of 2 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)"
- `pnpm check:new-line-citations`: `VERDICT new-cross-file-line-citations: 0 new citation(s)`
- `pnpm check:control-bytes`: OK
- changeset-guard (`check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-overwrite`, `check-changeset-fixed`): all ✅
- `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`: ✅
- `check-vi-mock-specifiers`, `check-vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:test-path-roots`: OK
- `check:unreferenced-sources`: "Every shipped source file in every covered package is reachable"
- `check-shell-escape-residue`: OK
- `check-doc-links`, `check-doc-fence-languages`, `check-doc-example-ids`, `check:i18n-keys`, `check:i18n-dead-keys`: exit 0
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the 12 changed paths: "NOT GOVERNED"

**Lint, a proven narrowing:**

- **Population:** read from the root `eslint.config.js`, which neither package overrides. All 8 existing changed files are linted and none is ignored.
- **Count:** `--format json` reports 8 files, 0 errors.
- **Invariance:**
  - No rule is type-aware: no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService` in the config.
  - No rule in `eslint-rules/` reads the filesystem, and there is no import-resolution plugin.
  - So this diff cannot move any other file's verdict.
- **Warnings:** the 36 warnings match the base versions of the same two files exactly (base leg re-linted, then restored and byte-checked). They are `react-refresh/only-export-components` ×2, `no-explicit-any` ×29, `set-state-in-effect` ×4 and `preserve-manual-memoization` ×1, none on a changed line.

**Not measured locally:** `performance-budget` (`check:eager-closure`) needs a full console `vite build` and is left to CI. The diff removes one lazily-loaded chunk and adds no import.

## In-place comment fixes outside the claimed file surface

`packages/app-shell/src/layout/__tests__/systemNavSettingsTarget.test.tsx` and `systemNavDatasourcesHop.test.tsx` are not in the claim's file list. Their comments became false when this change landed: one said `system` → `SystemHubPage`, and the other pointed at the deleted `SystemHubPage.metadataCards.test.tsx`. The edit is comment-only, and all four conditions for a bounded in-place fix hold:

1. Same class: dangling references to the retired page.
2. The edit is mechanical.
3. The open-PR file lists read this session show no other PR touching either file.
4. Same gate family: the app-shell vitest set above covers both files.

## Acceptance notes (not filed)

- `.claude/skills/objectui-contributor/guides/console-development.md` still describes `SystemHubPage`: the page tree, the host route table, and the "Adding a new admin surface → Default answer" section, which quotes its `@deprecated` docblock. The "Retired names" table does not list it yet. This file is governed surface, so it needs its own PR. Carrier: the seat.
- `skills/objectui/guides/project-setup.md` still names a "system hub" among the console patterns. Governed surface. No carrier.
- `ROADMAP.md` has checklist lines that name `SystemHubPage`; two are now false (`/system/` → SystemHubPage, and "only `SystemHubPage`'s is still in the tree"). The file is outside the claim. No carrier.
- In both sidebars, `sys-settings` ("System Settings") now reaches the same page as `sys-config` ("Configuration"), one redirect hop later. The senders keep `/apps/setup/system` on purpose: app-shell is host-agnostic, and the `system` segment is whatever landing the host declares. Re-pointing or merging those entries is a separate choice. No carrier.
- `AppContent.pseudoRouteSegments.test.tsx` still names its host stub for `/apps/setup/system` `system-hub-page`. It is a stub test id with no behaviour behind it. No carrier.
